incidente.resumo: On July 18, 2013, a network connectivity loss made all of Twilio's billing Redis slaves request full synchronization at once, overloading the master; a restart then made it read an incorrect configuration file, drop all balance data and boot read-only, so auto-recharge repeatedly charged credit cards of 1.4% of customers without updating balances. The billing system was taken offline, balances were restored from a separate double-bookkeeping datastore, and billing was progressively re-enabled the next day.

descricao.texto: At 2:42 AM PDT the monitoring system alerted the on-call engineering team of a failure in the Redis cluster; at 3:28 AM PDT billing system monitoring reported anomalous activity.
trechos: At 2:42 AM PDT, our monitoring system alerted our on-call engineering team of a failure in the Redis cluster.
At 3:28 AM PDT, the billing system monitoring reported the anomalous activity.

gatilho.texto: Observing extreme load on the host, the redis process on redis-master was misdiagnosed as requiring a restart, and on-call engineers restarted redis-master at 2:42 AM PDT to address the high load.
trechos: Observing extreme load on the host, the redis process on redis-master was misdiagnosed as requiring a restart to recover.
2:42 AM PDT / 9:42 UTC: Our on-call engineers restarted the redis-master to address the high load.

descricao.texto: On restart, redis-master read an incorrect configuration file, which made Redis attempt to recover from a non-existent AOF file instead of the binary snapshot, dropping all balance data, and made redis-master boot as a slave of itself in read-only mode, preventing the billing system from updating account balances.
trechos: This caused redis-master to read an incorrect configuration file, which in turn caused Redis to attempt to recover from a non-existent AOF file, instead of the binary snapshot. As a result of that failed recovery, redis-master dropped all balance data.

In addition to forcing recovery from a non-existent AOF, an incorrect configuration also caused redis-master to boot as a slave of itself, putting it in read-only mode and preventing the billing system from updating account balances.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: At 1:35 AM PDT a loss of network connectivity made all billing redis-slaves disconnect and simultaneously request full synchronization with the master, causing extreme load, performance degradation and timeouts; by 2:39 AM PDT services relying on redis-master began to fail.
trechos: At 1:35 AM PDT on July 18, a loss of network connectivity caused all billing redis-slaves to simultaneously disconnect from the master. This caused all redis-slaves to reconnect and request full synchronization with the master at the same time.
Receiving full sync requests from each redis-slave caused the master to suffer extreme load, resulting in performance degradation of the master and timeouts from redis-slaves to redis-master.
By 2:39 AM PDT the host’s load became so extreme, services relying on redis-master began to fail.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The auto-recharge system failed dangerously: with balances at zero and read-only, billable usage triggered recharges on customers' credit cards, which were charged without the balances being updated, so cards were charged repeatedly; only accounts with auto-recharge enabled were affected.
trechos: With all account balances at zero and read-only, Twilio usage that resulted in a billing transaction (e.g. 1 cent for a SMS message or a phone call) triggered the billing system to attempt a recharge using the credit card associated with the customer’s account. This only affected accounts with auto-recharge enabled.
Consequently, the billing system charged customer credit cards to increase account balances without being able to update the balances themselves.

The simultaneous loss of in-flight balance data and the ability to update balances also exposed a critical flaw in our auto-recharge system. It failed dangerously, exposing customer accounts to incorrect charges and suspensions.

passos.texto: At 4:10 AM PDT the billing system was taken offline to prevent further credit card charges.
trechos: At 4:10 AM PDT, on-call engineers responding to the incident shut down the billing system to prevent further charges.

passos.texto: At 6:24 AM PDT service was restored to all suspended accounts.
trechos: 6:24 AM PDT / 13:24 UTC: Service restored to all suspended accounts.

passos.texto: Account balances lost in the failed redis-master recovery were restored from the independent double-bookkeeping record in a separate relational datastore, and the billing system was turned on at 11:58 AM PDT.
trechos: The billing system maintains independent double-bookkeeping for all balance data in a separate relational datastore. Following the shutdown of the billing system, this independent record was used to restore the account balances lost in the failed recovery of the redis-master.
Once these balances were properly restored, the billing system was turned on at 11:58 AM PDT.

passos.texto: After the recurrence at 12:36 PM PDT, the billing system was taken offline again and suspended accounts were immediately reactivated.
trechos: 12:36 PM PDT / 19:36 UTC: Monitoring detected a recurrence of the original billing anomalies, affecting another 0.3% of all Twilio customers. The billing system was taken offline again. Suspended accounts were immediately reactivated.

passos.texto: The original redis cluster was replaced while resolving the incident.
trechos: In the process of resolving the incident, we replaced the original redis cluster that triggered the incident.

passos.texto: On July 19 the billing system was activated progressively for groups of customer accounts from 7:10 PM PDT, for all customers at 8:14 PM PDT, and the all-clear was given at 9:15 PM PDT.
trechos: 7:10 PM PDT / July 20 02:30 UTC: The billing system was activated progressively for groups of customer accounts.
8:14 PM PDT / July 20 03:14 UTC: The billing system was activated for all customers.
9:15 PM PDT / July 20 04:15 UTC: We gave the all-clear message, and all systems were restored.

acoes.texto: Already done: the incorrect configuration for redis-master was identified and corrected.
trechos: The incorrect configuration for redis-master was identified and corrected.

acoes.texto: Already done: Redis restarts on redis-master are disabled, and future redis-master recoveries will be done by pivoting a slave.
trechos: As a further preventative measure, Redis restarts on redis-master are disabled and future redis-master recoveries will be accomplished by pivoting a slave.

acoes.texto: In progress: fail-safes in the auto-recharge path so that if billing balances do not exist or cannot be written, the system will not suspend accounts or charge credit cards.
trechos: We are now introducing robust fail-safes, so that if billing balances don’t exist or cannot be written, the system will not suspend accounts or charge credit cards.

acoes.texto: Planned: update the billing system to validate against the double-bookkeeping databases in real time.
trechos: Finally, we will be updating the billing system to validate against our double-bookkeeping databases in real-time.

observacoes: categoria_causa is human-error following the operator-action rule: the misdiagnosed restart is the gatilho and the incorrect configuration file is the causa_raiz. duracao is null because the end time is ambiguous: the timeline gives the all-clear at 9:15 PM PDT on July 19, while the Root Cause section says full restoration was reached 'at 9:15 AM PDT' the following day; candidate start times are 1:35 AM PDT (network loss), 2:39 AM PDT (services failing) and 3:28 AM PDT (billing anomaly detected). The summary says 1.4% of customers were affected; the timeline gives 1.1% and then another 0.3%. Refunds for erroneous charges were processed from 2:57 PM PDT on July 18 to 3:00 PM PDT on July 19, and impacted accounts received a 10% credit. The text says the incorrect configuration file existed but not when it was introduced. After billing was turned back on at 11:58 AM PDT, monitoring detected a recurrence of the anomalies at 12:36 PM PDT affecting another 0.3% of customers.
